1. Assessment: CONSISTENT.

2. Evidence: The strongest apparent conflict is between the bronze swallow being fixed in the sealed case and later references to “Return” moving or being given away.

Relevant passages:

> “One was bronze… The other was plaster painted the same dark brown.”

> “At nine the archivist wrapped the bronze swallow and sealed it in a transparent case…”

> “The bronze stayed inside… behind its intact seal…”

> “During the ceremony, Iona lifted the plaster swallow from the counter and placed it in the teacher’s open bag.”

There is no contradiction because the story distinguishes the two birds clearly. The bronze remains sealed and later collected by the archivist; the plaster bird is the one touched by the porter and given to the teacher. The shared name “Return” creates possible confusion, but the text repeatedly specifies which physical object is involved.

3. Strongest alternative reading: One could read “People kept calling both birds Return” as deliberately blurring the identities of the two swallows, perhaps making it seem that “Return” both stayed in the case and left in the teacher’s bag. The text does not support that as a factual contradiction, because it keeps the bronze/plaster distinction explicit at each action point.

4. Minimal repair: No repair needed.

5. Other plausible continuity problem or editing seam: The final line reveals that Iona goes home “with the mould wrapped in her mother’s apron,” though the opening only says the swallows were “cast from her mother’s mould,” not that Iona brought the mould to the station. This is mildly abrupt but not inconsistent; the mould could have been present off-page.

6. Confidence: High. I see no incompatible fixed facts, only a deliberate doubling of name, material, and memory.
